rationale: Focused epigenetic KO sort screen (542 guides on 78 genes plus reporter and control guides; 30 safe-harbor negative controls (AAVS1, CCR5, ROSA26)) in HT29 SOX9-mKate2/KRT20-GFP dual endogenous reporter CRC cells. The deposited read-count matrix (Epigenetic_Screen_2) is transposed (guides in columns); it was transposed so guides are rows and the 36 sample columns are L1-L6 x fractions F1-F5(+unknown). The Epigenetic_Screen_Design sheet maps Gate2 libraries L3 (Rep1) and L6 (Rep2) to the dual-reporter 4-way sort: L3 F1=GFP,F2=DP/++,F3=DN/--,F4=mCh ; L6 F1=DN/--,F2=GFP,F3=mCh,F4=DP/++. The paper's key dual-reporter comparison (Fig 3d-e, MAGeCK-MLE beta score) is GFPhigh/mKate2low (differentiated) vs mKate2high/GFPlow (stem); reproduced as GFP vs mCh across the two Gate2 replicates (2 vs 2, 1 residual df). Enriched in GFP = induces differentiation (the paper's SMARCB1 and differentiation regulators; SOX9 sgRNAs are the positive control). DN vs DP is a secondary contrast. Only 2 replicates are deposited although the paper reports 3 technical replicates, and there are only 30 negative-control guides, so the test cannot be calibrated and no control null can be built; FDRs are nominal and these are low-power screening-level calls. Two single-reporter quartile contrasts are added to match the paper's MAGeCK-MLE beta comparisons (top vs bottom 25%): KRT20-GFP high vs low (L1/L4, differentiation inducers enriched in GFP-high) and SOX9-mKate2 high vs low (L2/L5, SOX9 suppressors depleted in mKate2-high); F1 and F4 are taken as the extreme quartiles (orientation not stated in the deposit, so the sign may be flipped).
